cohort: Children aged 1.5 to 10 years from the community were screened for autism spectrum disorder and assessed for associated antenatal and neonatal risk factors.
finding: Children diagnosed with ASD had significantly higher odds of having mothers with pregnancy-induced hypertension and bleeding per vaginum during pregnancy, and experiencing birth asphyxia, cardiorespiratory problems, metabolic abnormalities, and neonatal sepsis compared to controls.
followup_time: Up to 10 years (outcome assessed at this age range relative to antenatal/neonatal exposures)
